elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The line shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. Debt fluctuated, peaking around 2021 before falling to 397.8 in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations
elements.description: The stacked bars break down 2025 external debt by debt type, creditor type and individual creditors. Public and publicly guaranteed debt is the largest top-level category at US$298.2 million, while private nonguaranteed debt is the smallest at US$16.7 million. World Bank-IDA is the largest listed multilateral creditor, and China is the larger bilateral creditor.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (light shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show debt ratios from 2015 to 2025 against the shaded range of reporting countries. External debt relative to exports has a pronounced mid-period peak, while the other ratios fluctuate more moderately. In 2025, external debt relative to exports is the highest displayed ratio at 101%, and debt service relative to GNI is the lowest at 3%.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes show Official creditors and Private creditors. Each box lists Maturity, Grace period and Interest rate, all marked '..'; no arrows are shown. No values are available because the country had no new commitments in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for official or private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
